one_line_contribution: The claim is that an optimized instruction and a retrieved memory item are informational substitutes at the level of a specific clause-item pair, tested causally by deleting the one instruction clause a retrieved item duplicates and showing that this — but not deleting a length-matched unrelated clause — restores the item's marginal value; the k*-shrinkage grid is the observational wrapper around that mechanism test.
closest_prior_work: The proposal itself names MemMachine (arXiv:2604.04853) as pre-empting the observation, and correctly retreats to mechanism. The more dangerous neighbour it does not confront is the instruction-vs-demonstration substitution already visible inside the prompt-optimization literature it cites: MIPROv2's own ablations report that instruction optimization and bootstrapped demonstrations are largely non-additive, with instruction search paying off mainly on tasks whose conditional rules the demonstrations fail to convey — which is the substitution claim in the demonstration slot, one abstraction step from this proposal's memory slot. Stack that on Min et al.'s finding that demonstrations contribute format and label space more than content, plus FILCO/RECOMP/MMR redundancy filtering and the lost-in-the-middle distractor line for the harm side, and the conceptual space is crowded enough that the surviving delta is narrow: 'the conditioning variable for redundancy should be the instruction clause, not the query or the other items.' That is a real delta, but it is a refinement, not a new phenomenon, and the proposal argues for it against MemMachine only, never against MIPROv2's non-additivity result.
strongest_objection: P2, the load-bearing prediction, does not test the claim that makes the paper interesting. E4's DiD compares (B-B0)-(A-A0) against (C-C0)-(A-A0): deleting clause c(m*) removes procedural information from the instruction, and m* re-supplies it. A positive DiD therefore follows from plain additive information accounting — content that supplies missing information helps more when the information is missing — and is close to tautological given how m* is selected (max redundancy against c(m*)). What substitution needs, and what the pilot and the k* story actually assert, is that a duplicated item has *negative* marginal value under the full instruction, i.e. arm A < A0 beyond the noise floor. Sub-additivity down to zero marginal value cannot move argmax-k from {4,8} to {0,1,2}; only a positive interference cost can. The plan never pre-registers a sign test on A-A0, so the 'ceiling/saturation killer' can pass cleanly while the harm claim — the entire motivation — goes untested. A reviewer will also note that if A-A0 is near zero (the likely case, since these are the most redundant items), the DiD reduces to 'B beats A', which is just the confound the placebo arm C was meant to remove being reintroduced through the selection rule.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes, none of which need more budget. (1) Add to P2 a necessary condition: high-R items must show negative marginal value under I3 (A significantly below A0 against the E3 null floor); report the DiD as uninterpretable for the substitution claim if A-A0 >= 0, since a positive DiD with a non-negative A-A0 is ordinary information restoration. (2) Add an instruction-side length placebo to the E1 ladder — I0 padded to I3-s1's token count with non-procedural filler, and/or a clause-scrambled I3 — so the k-slope difference is attributable to procedural content rather than instruction length, position, or specificity. E2 pads the memory but nothing pads the instruction, and I_H controls only for GEPA provenance, not length. (3) Move the MIPROv2 bootstrapped-demonstration arm at matched k out of the conditional Tier 3 and into Tier 1: without it the paper cannot say whether substitution is about self-edited memory or about any in-context exemplar. (4) Run the promised >=15-query search before committing the design, not before submission; and pre-register how uncertainty on argmax-k is computed (bootstrap over items), since 'argmax moved regime' is currently an unquantified conjunct of P1.
missing_baseline: A length-matched non-procedural instruction (I0 inflated to I3-s1's token count with generic, task-relevant-sounding but non-procedural text) crossed with k, plus a clause-scrambled variant of I3-s1. Every instruction-level contrast in E1 confounds procedural content with instruction length and specificity, and E2's padding is applied to the memory slot only, so nothing in Tier 1 rules out 'longer instructions leave less usable attention for injected context.' Secondary omission: the MIPROv2 bootstrapped-demonstration arm at matched k, which is the control separating 'self-edited memory substitutes for instructions' from 'any demonstrations substitute for instructions', is parked in E8 and runs only if Tiers 1-2 are already positive — i.e. the discriminating control is conditional on the result it is supposed to discriminate.
preprint_collision: The check is, by the proposal's own admission, empty: the search tool failed on every attempt and this round contributes no new collision evidence. Honesty about that is creditable but it is not a substitute for having searched, and per the standard that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness, this costs the proposal. The carried-forward list comes from an earlier five-query-capped search, and the newest items cited are 2603/2604 identifiers — roughly four to six months stale in a field the proposal itself argues moves in preprint time; the entire recent window is unexamined. I cannot verify any of the cited identifiers here, so the collision status must be read as unknown rather than clear. The named risk is specific and live: if MemMachine or a successor already reports an item-level or clause-level causal probe of the prompt-retrieval interaction, the surviving delta collapses to the noise-floor-referenced effect sizes, which is a workshop-scale contribution. The commitment to re-search before submission is the wrong sequencing — a collision found then invalidates experiments already run, so the search belongs before Tier 1, and the proposal should say so.
